launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.description: The popular 32nd Street Beach on Bde Maka Ska has sand, open-water swimming, lake paths, and nearby rentals; check daily water-quality and lifeguard status.
Lake Harriet Bandshell anchors free seasonal concerts and movies beside the pavilion, playground, paths, docks, and Bread & Pickle concession.
Lake Harriet North Beach is a smaller neighborhood swimming area on the lake's north shore; beach supervision and water testing are seasonal.
Lake of the Isles offers a scenic separated walking and biking loop, fishing, winter skating and ski routes, and connections toward Cedar Lake and Bde Maka Ska.
Cedar Lake East Beach is a quieter beach reached from parkway and trail connections, with fewer nearby services than the largest lake destinations.
Cedar Lake Point Beach is a small neighborhood-scale swimming destination; verify water quality and arrive by bike or foot when nearby parking is tight.
Lyndale Park Rose Garden is a free formal garden near Lake Harriet with seasonal blooms, fountains, paths, and wedding activity.
The heritage Como-Harriet Streetcar operates seasonally near Lake Harriet; it is a separately scheduled and ticketed experience, not ordinary transit.

launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.description: The 53-foot falls are viewed from accessible upper overlooks; lower viewpoints require stairs and gorge paths that become wet, icy, or closed.
Sea Salt Eatery operates seasonally beside the falls pavilion with seafood, drinks, and long peak-time lines; park access does not guarantee restaurant service.
Lower Glen Trail follows Minnehaha Creek toward the Mississippi through steep, shaded gorge terrain with stairs, roots, mud, and limited facilities.
Wabun combines an accessible playground, seasonal wading pool, picnic facilities, disc golf, and a river overlook in the park's southeastern zone.
Longfellow Gardens sit above the highway tunnel across from the main park, offering free formal plantings and a quieter wedding setting.
Longfellow House is a historic replica near the gardens; exhibits and interior access depend on current staffing and program hours.
The restored Princess Depot stands near the falls and Pergola Garden; interior interpretation is seasonal while the exterior remains visible.
The Hiawatha and Minnehaha sculpture sits on a small island above the falls and is viewed from the creek edge, not entered or climbed.

launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.description: The Trailhead is the central orientation, restroom, rental, event, and year-round recreation building, with independent food and activity schedules.
Wirth Lake Beach provides seasonal swimming, fishing, nearby parking, and access to cycling trails; verify water quality and lifeguard status.
Eloise Butler is a seasonal native wildflower garden and bird sanctuary with a visitor shelter, natural paths, and separate opening dates.
Quaking Bog is reached by a short boardwalk through a sensitive wetland; remain on the route and expect a small metered lot with seasonal access.
JD Rivers Children's Garden hosts youth gardening and food programs; plots are educational spaces rather than public picking gardens.
More than five miles of shared off-road trails range from beginner to expert and close to every user when wet enough to leave tracks.
The Par 3 golf and 18-hole disc-golf area is separately operated with fees or activity rules and a distinct parking area.
Winter recreation includes groomed skiing, snowshoeing, tubing, snowboarding, and fat biking; passes, rentals, snow conditions, and route rules vary daily.

launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.description: Winchell Trail is the west-bank natural-surface bluff trail, with roots, slopes, ravines, stairs, and multiple neighborhood access points.
East River Flats provides developed river access below the University of Minnesota, with event lawns, boat activity, paths, and seasonal facilities.
Bohemian Flats is a west-bank river lawn and launch area below Washington Avenue, used for events and regional trail connections.
Franklin Avenue Bridge offers broad gorge views from pedestrian sidewalks; traffic, wind, construction, and bridge approaches affect comfort.
The 36th Street gorge stairs descend from West River Parkway toward Winchell Trail; expect long steps, no elevator, and seasonal ice or closures.
The 44th Street stairs connect bluff-top neighborhoods to lower gorge routes and require a return climb with no nearby restroom.
The paved regional trail follows river parkways for biking, walking, and mobility access, with bridge connections between banks.
Riverside Park is a developed neighborhood gateway above the west bank with recreation space and connections toward gorge trails.

launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.description: Spoonbridge and Cherry is the garden's iconic centerpiece over a shallow ornamental pond; view from paths and do not enter the water or climb the artwork.
Katharina Fritsch's bright blue Hahn/Cock stands in the lower garden and is viewed from accessible central paths.
James Turrell's Sky Pesher is a below-grade viewing chamber; access can be affected by weather, maintenance, and posted artwork rules.
Woodrow is a large bronze horse sculpture integrated with the garden landscape; use the digital guide for current interpretation.
Theaster Gates's Black Vessel for a Saint combines sculpture and contemplative space in the garden's current collection.
Sol LeWitt's X with Columns creates a geometric open structure; paths and sightlines provide multiple views without climbing.
Wurtele Upper Garden is reached by an accessible switchback route and connects sculpture, skyline views, and Walker entrances across the hillside.
Walker Art Center is the adjacent ticketed museum with restrooms, cafe, visitor help, galleries, film, and performances during shorter indoor hours.

launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.description: Como Park Zoo is free with donations encouraged and keeps independent daily hours, animal-building schedules, visitor rules, and occasional exhibit closures.
The free conservatory includes tropical and seasonal plant rooms with independent hours, indoor humidity, stroller flow, and temporary room closures.
The Japanese Garden is a seasonal landscaped space associated with the conservatory; opening and event access can differ from the general park.
Como Lakeside Pavilion provides lake views, music, food, rentals, and event space on a separately operated schedule.
Como Town is a seasonal amusement park beside the zoo with separately purchased rides and weather-dependent operation.
Cafesjian's Carousel is a separately ticketed historic ride with its own season and hours near the zoo and amusement area.
Como Regional Park Pool is a seasonal paid aquatic center with supervised pools, slides, admission rules, and daily safety breaks.
Como Woodland Outdoor Classroom offers free interpretive trails through restored habitats away from the busiest zoo campus.

launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.description: The free guarded sand beach operates seasonally and weather permitting with changing rooms, restrooms, rentals, and youth supervision rules.
The free beach splash pad is scheduled 9:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. June 13-September 7 in 2026, subject to maintenance and weather closures.
Phalen China Garden is a free cultural landscape and pavilion area intended for respectful walking, viewing, and community events.
The reservable picnic pavilion and nearby island include tables, grills, shelter, and a designated fire pit under permit rules.
The outdoor amphitheater hosts music and community events; setup and reservations can close seating or nearby paths.
Phalen Golf Course is separately operated with fees, tee times, clubhouse services, and boundaries that are not general park space.
The north-side boat launch serves non-motorized and permitted lake access; rentals and storage are coordinated separately through beach operations.
The roughly three-mile paved loop is shared by walkers and cyclists and links beach, garden, picnic, fishing, and recreation zones.

launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.description: The 5,000-square-foot Wigington Pavilion is a historic reservable event building; private rentals do not provide general public interior access.
Target Stage hosts concerts and festivals on the main event lawn, with temporary fencing, sound equipment, and access changes during setup.
Kelley's Landing is a reservable riverside picnic shelter with its own capacity, parking, and permit conditions.
The public dock provides direct Mississippi access without lifeguards; river current, wake, debris, flooding, and temporary closures require caution.
The paved riverwalk frames downtown skyline views and connects lawns, docks, trails, and neighboring riverfront destinations.
The play area serves family visits near lawns and picnic space; supervise closely because the river and event traffic are nearby.
Raspberry Island sits under the Wabasha Bridge with a bandshell, trails, and downtown access; it is a related riverfront destination across the channel.
Padelford Riverboats board sightseeing cruises from Harriet Island on a separately ticketed, seasonal schedule with specific arrival requirements.
